102: function powershellScript(ordered: string[]): string {
103:   const lines: string[] = [];
104:   lines.push("$ErrorActionPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'");
105:   lines.push('$candidates = @(');
106:   for (const id of ordered) {

112:   lines.push('$exe = $null');
113:   lines.push('foreach ($c in $candidates) { if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $c.exe) { $exe = $c.exe; break } }');
114:   lines.push("if (-not $exe) { Write-Host 'No supported player found. Install one of: VLC / MPV / MPC-HC / PotPlayer, then run this again.' -ForegroundColor Red; exit 1 }");
115:   lines.push("$dir = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'MovieDownloader'");
116:   lines.push('New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dir | Out-Null');
117:   lines.push("$wrap = Join-Path $dir 'movie-open.cmd'");
118:   lines.push("$batch = @( '@echo off', 'set \"arg=%1\"', 'set \"arg=%arg:*movie://=%\"', 'start \"\" \"__EXE__\" \"%arg%\"' )");
119:   lines.push('$body = ([string]::Join([Environment]::NewLine, $batch)).Replace(\'__EXE__\', $exe)');
120:   lines.push('Set-Content -Path $wrap -Value $body -Encoding ASCII');
121:   lines.push("$key = 'HKCU:\\Software\\Classes\\movie\\shell\\open\\command'");
122:   lines.push('New-Item -Path $key -Force | Out-Null');
123:   lines.push('$regValue = \'"\' + $wrap + \'" "%1"\'');
124:   lines.push("Set-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name '(default)' -Value $regValue");
125:   lines.push('Write-Host ("Registered movie:// -> " + $exe) -ForegroundColor Green');

130: /** Encode a PowerShell command for -EncodedCommand (UTF-16LE, base64). */
131: function encodePsCommand(source: string): string {
132:   const bytes = new Uint8Array(source.length * 2);
133:   for (let i = 0; i < source.length; i += 1) {
134:     const code = source.charCodeAt(i);
135:     bytes[i * 2] = code & 0xff;
136:     bytes[i * 2 + 1] = (code >> 8) & 0xff;

139:   const chunk = 0x8000;
140:   for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += chunk) {
141:     binary += String.fromCharCode(...bytes.subarray(i, i + chunk));

174:   const ordered = orderedPlayerIds(preferred, LINUX_ORDER);
175:   const lines: string[] = [];
176:   lines.push('#!/bin/sh');
177:   lines.push('# Movie Downloader - one-time local-player setup (Linux).');
178:   lines.push('# Registers the movie:// scheme so the "Player" buttons open files');
179:   lines.push('# in your installed media player. Requires xdg-utils (Ubuntu ships it).');

181:   lines.push('');
182:   lines.push('launcher=');
183:   lines.push('player_name=');
184:   lines.push('');
185:   lines.push('probe() {');
186:   lines.push('  [ -n "$launcher" ] && return 0');
187:   lines.push('  bin=$(command -v "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)');
188:   lines.push('  if [ -n "$bin" ]; then');
189:   lines.push('    launcher="$bin"');
190:   lines.push('    player_name="$2"');
191:   lines.push('    return 0');
192:   lines.push('  fi');
193:   lines.push('  if [ "$#" -ge 3 ] && command -v flatpak >/dev/null 2>&1 && flatpak info "$3" >/dev/null 2>&1; then');
194:   lines.push('    launcher="flatpak run $3"');
195:   lines.push('    player_name="$2"');
196:   lines.push('  fi');
197:   lines.push('}');
198:   lines.push('');
199:   for (const id of ordered) {
200:     const p = LINUX_PLAYERS[id];
201:     if (p) lines.push(`probe "${p.cmd}" "${p.name}" "${p.flatpak}"`);
202:   }
203:   lines.push('');
204:   lines.push('if [ -z "$launcher" ]; then');
205:   lines.push('  echo "No supported player found. Install VLC or MPV, then run this again." >&2');
206:   lines.push('  exit 1');
207:   lines.push('fi');
208:   lines.push('');
209:   lines.push('echo "Using $player_name ($launcher)"');
210:   lines.push('');
211:   lines.push('dir="$HOME/.local/share/movie-downloader"');
212:   lines.push('appdir="$HOME/.local/share/applications"');
213:   lines.push('mkdir -p "$dir"');
214:   lines.push('mkdir -p "$appdir"');
215:   lines.push('');
216:   lines.push('cat > "$dir/movie-open.sh" <<\'EOF\'');
217:   lines.push('#!/bin/sh');
218:   lines.push('url=${1#movie://}');
219:   lines.push('[ -n "$url" ] || exit 1');
220:   lines.push('nohup __LAUNCHER__ "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 &');
221:   lines.push('EOF');
222:   lines.push('sed -i "s|__LAUNCHER__|$launcher|" "$dir/movie-open.sh"');
223:   lines.push('chmod +x "$dir/movie-open.sh"');
224:   lines.push('');
225:   lines.push('desktop="$appdir/movie-downloader.desktop"');

238:   lines.push('xdg-mime default movie-downloader.desktop x-scheme-handler/movie >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "Could not set the default handler; pick Movie Downloader player for movie:// in your desktop settings." >&2');
239:   lines.push('if command -v update-desktop-database >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-desktop-database "$appdir" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi');
240:   lines.push('');
241:   lines.push('echo "Registered movie:// -> $player_name ($launcher)"');

9:

# Plan — Master Index & Doc Architecture

This document defines **how this planning set is structured** and how it will be executed. It is the entry point for any human or agent reading this repo.

## Project

- **Name:** `noAir` (GitHub repo `noair-movie-downloader`)
- **One-line purpose:** Self-hosted web app that searches movies/TV via TMDB, finds torrent/magnet sources via Prowlarr, downloads them with qBittorrent (Docker), shows live download progress, and plays the finished video in-browser (or hands it to the user's local player).

## Goal of this doc set

Produce a complete, unambiguous blueprint so that:

- A human can review the entire plan in under 15 minutes.
- An agent can execute the whole build top-to-bottom **without making design decisions**.
- Every task has a verifiable "done" condition.

## Doc layout

```
AGENTS.md                        # Project rules, commands, conventions — always read first
docs/plan/
  00-index.md                    # THIS FILE — overview, build order, locked decisions
  01-architecture.md             # System design: components, data flow, boundaries
  02-specs.md                    # Concrete contracts: API, data model, UI, providers
  03-tasks.md                    # Ordered, numbered milestones w/ acceptance criteria
```

## What each doc is FOR (and what it is NOT for)

| File | Contains | Must NOT contain |
|------|----------|------------------|
| `AGENTS.md` | Repo-level rules, run commands, edit conventions, pointer to this index | Project design decisions |
| `00-index.md` | Scope, goals, **locked decisions**, build order, conventions for the docs themselves | Implementation detail |
| `01-architecture.md` | Components, responsibilities, data flow diagrams, tech boundaries, what talks to what | Line-by-line implementation |
| `02-specs.md` | Concrete contracts: endpoints + payloads, schema, UI screens/flows, provider interfaces | Rationale, alternatives, opinions |
| `03-tasks.md` | Numbered tasks in build order; each with inputs, outputs, acceptance criteria | Design discussion |

## Rules for writing every doc

1. **Decisions, not options.** Every "we could use X or Y" becomes "we use X." No open choices left for the executor.
2. **Requirements + acceptance criteria, not prose.** Facts an agent can verify. No ambiguous adjectives.
3. **One fact lives in one place.** If two docs disagree, the doc that "owns" it wins (ownership table below). Cross-reference instead of duplicating.
4. **Precise naming.** All names are written exactly once in `02-specs.md` and reused verbatim everywhere else.
5. **No "later"/"TBD" in a doc that the executor reads.** Anything unknown is recorded in this file under Open Questions, resolved, then moved into the relevant doc.

## Ownership table (single source of truth)

| Topic | Owned by |
|-------|----------|
| Tech stack, scope, build order | `00-index.md` |
| Components and data flow | `01-architecture.md` |
| API contracts, data model, UI, provider behavior | `02-specs.md` |
| Milestones, task order, acceptance criteria | `03-tasks.md` |

## Locked decisions

| # | Decision |
|---|----------|
| D1 | Backend: **Node.js + Express 4 + TypeScript**. Single-user app, no auth. |
| D2 | Frontend: **React 18 + Vite + TypeScript**, React Router, **Zustand** for client state, plain CSS (no UI framework). |
| D3 | Database: **PostgreSQL 16 as a Docker service** (named volume), `pg` driver, schema run on backend boot. |
| D4 | Torrent indexer: **Prowlarr (Docker)**. One normalized search API; trackers (TPB, 1337x, etc.) configured in Prowlarr, not in code. |
| D5 | Downloader: **qBittorrent (Docker)** via its Web API v2. Backend polls it every 2s. |
| D6 | Metadata + imagery: **TMDB API** (free key). All poster/backdrop images proxied by the backend so the key never reaches the browser. |
| D7 | Realtime UI updates: **Socket.IO**. Server pushes a full downloads snapshot every 2s. |
| D8 | Playback: **play only after the file is fully downloaded**. qBittorrent writes in-progress files as `x.mkv.!qb` and renames them when complete; the backend never lists or serves `.!qb` files, so `stream_file_path`/`streamable` appear only once a complete file exists (inside a season pack, individually-completed episodes unlock early). Completed files are served over HTTP **Range** (`/api/stream/:infoHash`) for external players and browser-safe direct playback; `lib/streamPlan.ts` still routes browser-unsupported audio (→ AAC remux) and sub-4K HEVC (→ H.264 transcode) through ffmpeg for *completed* files, and 4K/UHD non-safe video to the external-player flow via the `movie://` scheme. Browser codec limits (H.264/VP9/AV1; no HEVC/.avi guarantee) still apply. `playinfo` also probes every audio/subtitle track for the browser-player upgrade. Packaging never re-encodes browser-safe AAC-LC audio (stream-copied) and runs renditions concurrently (S14); before packaging, Watch probes `mseProbe` codec strings and routes undecodable video (e.g. HEVC Main10) straight to the external-player screen. |
| D9 | Deployment: single `docker-compose.yml` with services `postgres`, `qbittorrent`, `prowlarr`, `backend`, `frontend`. Frontend served by nginx that proxies `/api` and `/socket.io` to the backend. |
| D10 | Cost: everything is free/open-source. Only required external account is a free TMDB API key; an **optional free OMDb key** (`OMDB_API_KEY`) enables portrait posters for the wide tiles (§4.6) — cards degrade to monograms when absent. |
| D11 | Testing: **Vitest** on the backend (unit tests with mocked providers); frontend smoke test via manual run in M4. |
| D12 | Magnet links: prefer Prowlarr-provided magnet; otherwise build from `infoHash` + 9 public trackers (list in `02-specs.md` §4.3). |
| D13 | LAN exposure: `frontend`, `qbittorrent` (Web UI), and `prowlarr` are all published on host ports (`0.0.0.0`). qBittorrent must have strong credentials (it has its own login); Prowlarr has no auth — documented risk accepted for a home LAN. `postgres` and `backend` stay internal-only. |
| D14 | TV browsing (v2): TV titles present TMDB **seasons/episodes**; contextual Prowlarr searches are whole-show (S3 no params), per-season (`?season=N` → season packs + episode releases), or per-episode (`?season=N&episode=M`). The Advanced picker retains the 30-row "Load more" + client-side filters/grouping from v1. **Friendly downloads auto-pick the most-seeded matching source**; releases with unparseable coverage are Advanced-only; a per-episode download never silently pulls a whole season. |
| D15 | Frontend visual language: **Netflix-style; black & white UI chrome over full-color artwork**. Left sidebar removed; fixed top header transparent at top that fades to a black gradient on scroll. Home = static cinematic brand hero + **16:9 full-bleed title-card tiles** (whole-card click, no captions/info icons) that bleed full-width with the rightmost card clipped to invite scroll; full-screen search overlay. Card art (superseded clause → **D21**): every tile is now the **OMDb-portrait composite** (no FanArt/TMDB imagery). Rail named "My Downloads"; **local-only playback resume** (C-DL2); **every friendly download opens a confirm sheet** naming the exact pick (C-DL1); **inline first-run guidance** (C-DL3). |
| D16 | TV metadata + episode columns: new `GET /api/media/:id/season/:n` (S12); `Source.coverage` from release titles with season gating on S3; downloads gain nullable `season_number`/`episode_number`/`backdrop_path` via idempotent `ALTER TABLE`; the file-list endpoint (S13) tags each file with season/episode server-side; `/watch/:infoHash?episode=SxxExx` auto-selects the matching file inside a season pack; the poll backfills season on legacy TV rows. |
| D17 | **~~Artwork pipeline v2 (poster-first tiles)~~ — SUPERSEDED by D21.** Kept for history: card identity is the poster, not the backdrop (Fanart/TMDB ladder, `art_files` cache, temporary `cardStyle` A/B). All of it (FanArt provider, enrichment, the Settings artwork controls) is **removed** by D21; only the `art_files` "poster on disk served via S8b" mechanism survived, re-sourced to OMDb. |
| D18 | **Hover-trailer previews — data layer**: every `TitleCard` resolves the title's best trailer for the hover card. Trailer metadata comes from TMDB `GET /movie/{id}/videos` / `GET /tv/{id}/videos` through the existing key — **no new key, no YouTube Data API, no backend storage** (`S15`). TV cards use the **series** trailer (per-episode trailers are not surfaced — TMDB coverage is sparse). The on-card presentation is **D20** (this entry no longer defines rendering). Embedding requires the *browser* to reach YouTube/Vimeo; the LAN box only needs TMDB reachability. |
| D19 | **Movie "the download is the loading screen" + version grouping**: the movie Detail hero renders one primary state (`DownloadsHeroPanel`) — no copy → Download best-match (inline "Best match · quality · size · seeds" hint, **Advanced**; shimmer while resolving) · copies arriving → status card (big tabular %, state, speed·ETA, Pause/Resume, Remove) · something playable → exactly one ▶ **Watch** (active version) + Player + delete with a **version-chip row** to switch, copies still downloading folded into mini-rows; **a disabled Watch is never rendered**. Best-source search runs only when the title owns no copy, is deduped + cached in the API client per context (~10 min), and lazily re-fetches after the last copy is deleted. Releases of one movie are **versions of a single library item** (`lib/versions.ts` pure helpers + `store/versionStore` persisted to `localStorage` keyed `movie:<tmdbId>`; default rule = most recently completed playable copy, tie-break higher resolution): My Downloads shows one card per movie with hover version chips; the Downloads page groups copies under `Movie · N versions` headers and labels each row `audio · quality`. Downloads persist `audioLang`/`audioMode` (idempotent `ALTER`, `S4`) so copies differing only by language stay distinguishable. TV keeps its episode layout and only reuses the panel for the active season pack; the C-DL1 confirm sheet is unchanged. |
| D20 | **Expanded Netflix-style hover card (replaces D18's inline overlay)**: every `TitleCard` expands into a **portaled, fixed pop-up card** after a sustained ~600 ms hover — width **1.7×** the base card (viewport-clamped), **vertically centered on the base cell (grows equally above and below)** and horizontally centered so it **overflows the neighbouring cards on all four sides**, `z-index: 150`, 8 px radius + strong dark shadow; base card keeps its grid slot (no white ring/scale while open); any scroll/resize dismisses it. Split layout: **media top (16:9)** = autoplay-looped trailer with **sound ON by default** (Chrome silences unmuted autoplay until the user has clicked the app once) + circular mute/unmute button that **remounts the iframe** (clip restarts), title/logo bottom-left over a scrim; **details bottom (dark column)** = compact Netflix-matching panel (16 px gutters, ~1.35 line-height, medium-500 13 px text): row 1 = Play (white circle → primary Watch action when present, else Detail) + two **decorative no-op circles** (Add to List `+`, Rate thumbs-up) + More Info chevron; My-Downloads version chips sit on their **own row beneath the actions**; row 2 = monochrome age-badge (`certification`) · duration ("2h 15m") or season count ("N Seasons") · `HD` chip (all 1 px translucent outlines, ~11 px); row 3 = up to three genre tags joined by `•`. Typeface is self-hosted **Inter Variable** (proprietary **Netflix Sans** is never bundled) standing in for the Netflix look. Data arrives from **S16** (`GET /api/media/:id/hover`), one call returning trailer + genres + runtime + seasons + certification, cached client-side ~1 h; US rating comes from TMDB `release_dates`/`content_ratings`. Every card expands even with no trailer (still artwork stands in); no pop-up for reduced-motion, `tmdbId <= 0`, or a failed/failed payload (static card). |
| D21 | **Netflix-style wide tiles from OMDb portraits — the winning card-art source.** Research: no free API serves *wide* per-title studio art except TMDB backdrops/FanArt (Netflix title cards are proprietary; OMDb returns only a portrait `Poster`). Decision: **wide 16:9 tile composited in-app from the OMDb portrait** — crisp portrait figure at full tile height over its own blurred ground; used everywhere (rails, My Downloads, downloads page, search, Detail hero as blurred ground). Pipeline: TMDB external_ids `imdbId` → OMDb (`OMDB_API_KEY`, budgeted ~850 req/day) → Amazon portrait downloaded once to the `art` volume (`art_files`, kind `poster`) → served by S8b, which **warms on first miss**; `empty` rows cached 7 days; no poster → monogram (never TMDB/FanArt imagery). **FanArt.tv and the whole artwork-settings cluster are deleted** (provider toggle, per-size preference, `cardStyle` A/B, preview tester, `ART_GRID` spike, `FANART_API_KEY`, `media_art`); `/api/settings` is audio-only; Settings shows no artwork controls. defapp_generic()
{
    MIME="$1"
    xdg_config_home="$XDG_CONFIG_HOME"
    [ -n "$xdg_config_home" ] || xdg_config_home="$HOME/.config"
    #shellcheck disable=SC2153 # not misspelled

    [ -n "$xdg_config_dirs" ] || xdg_config_dirs="/etc/xdg"
    xdg_user_dir="$XDG_DATA_HOME"
    [ -n "$xdg_user_dir" ] || xdg_user_dir="$HOME/.local/share"
    xdg_system_dirs="$XDG_DATA_DIRS"

    done

defapp_kde()
{
    MIME="$1"

      case "${KDE_SESSION_VERSION}" in

          KTRADER="$(command -v ktraderclient)" # FIXME: Plasma 6?

part.text: **Root cause found.** `new URL("movie://http://localhost:5173/api/stream/x")` canonicalizes to `movie://http//localhost:5173/...` — the WHATWG URI parser (used by every browser) drops the colon of the nested `http://` because it reads `http` as the *host* of the `movie` scheme. The wrapper then strips `movie://`, gets `http//localhost:5173/...` (no scheme → VLC treats it as a relative file path). #!/bin/sh
# noAir - one-time local-player setup (Linux).
#
# What this does (nothing hidden):
#   1. finds an installed player (your pick first: VLC, MPV)
#   2. writes a tiny launcher to ~/.local/share/movie-downloader/movie-open.sh
#   3. registers ~/.local/share/applications/movie-downloader.desktop as the
#      handler for movie:// links (xdg-mime x-scheme-handler/movie)
#   4. verifies the registration and prints the result
#
# It writes only the two files above and never touches your downloads.
# To undo: run the matching uninstaller, or:
#   rm ~/.local/share/applications/movie-downloader.desktop ~/.local/share/movie-downloader/movie-open.sh
set -u

launcher=
player_name=

probe() {
  [ -n "$launcher" ] && return 0
  bin=$(command -v "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$bin" ]; then
    launcher="$bin"
    player_name="$2"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "$#" -ge 3 ] && command -v flatpak >/dev/null 2>&1 && flatpak info "$3" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    launcher="flatpak run $3"
    player_name="$2"
  fi
}

probe "vlc" "VLC" "org.videolan.VLC"
probe "mpv" "MPV" "io.mpv.Mpv"

if [ -z "$launcher" ]; then
  echo "No supported player found. Install VLC or MPV, then run this again." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "Found: $player_name ($launcher)"

dir="$HOME/.local/share/movie-downloader"
appdir="$HOME/.local/share/applications"
mkdir -p "$dir"
mkdir -p "$appdir"

cat > "$dir/movie-open.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# noAir movie:// launcher. The desktop runs this with the full link as $1.
# Every browser re-serializes a link through its URI parser before handing
# it to the OS, so accept the shapes that reach us and normalize to http(s)://.
url=$1
case "$url" in
  movie://*) url=${url#movie://} ;;
  movie:*) url=${url#movie:} ;;
esac
case "$url" in
  //*) url=${url#//} ;;
esac
# Older builds embedded the stream URL as movie://http://host/...; URI parsers
# read "http" as the host and drop the colon (movie://http//host/...). Restore it.
case "$url" in
  http//*) url="http://${url#http//}" ;;
  https//*) url="https://${url#https//}" ;;
esac
case "$url" in
  http://*|https://*) ;;
  *) echo "movie-open: not an http(s) URL: $url" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
nohup __LAUNCHER__ "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
EOF
launcher_escaped=$(printf '%s' "$launcher" | sed 's/&/\\&/g')
sed -i "s|__LAUNCHER__|$launcher_escaped|" "$dir/movie-open.sh"
chmod +x "$dir/movie-open.sh"

desktop="$appdir/movie-downloader.desktop"
cat > "$desktop" <<EOF
[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Version=1.0
Name=Movie Downloader player
Comment=Open movie:// links from Movie Downloader
Exec="$dir/movie-open.sh" %u
Terminal=false
NoDisplay=true
MimeType=x-scheme-handler/movie;
EOF
chmod +x "$desktop"

xdg-mime default movie-downloader.desktop x-scheme-handler/movie >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "Could not set the default handler; pick Movie Downloader player for movie:// in your desktop settings." >&2
if command -v update-desktop-database >/dev/null 2>&1; then update-desktop-database "$appdir" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi

registered=$(xdg-mime query default x-scheme-handler/movie 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ "$registered" = "movie-downloader.desktop" ]; then
  echo "Verified: movie:// links now open $player_name."
else
  echo "Note: could not confirm the handler is the default yet." >&2
  echo "Check with: xdg-mime query default x-scheme-handler/movie" >&2
  echo "On GNOME you may need to log out and back in once after a first install." >&2
fi
echo "Done. The Player buttons in the app now open files in $player_name."

#!/bin/sh
# noAir movie:// launcher. The desktop runs this with the full link as $1.
# Every browser re-serializes a link through its URI parser before handing
# it to the OS, so accept the shapes that reach us and normalize to http(s)://.
url=$1
case "$url" in
  movie://*) url=${url#movie://} ;;
  movie:*) url=${url#movie:} ;;
esac
case "$url" in
  //*) url=${url#//} ;;
esac
# Older builds embedded the stream URL as movie://http://host/...; URI parsers
# read "http" as the host and drop the colon (movie://http//host/...). Restore it.
case "$url" in
  http//*) url="http://${url#http//}" ;;
  https//*) url="https://${url#https//}" ;;
esac
case "$url" in
  http://*|https://*) ;;
  *) echo "movie-open: not an http(s) URL: $url" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
nohup /usr/bin/vlc "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 &

part.text: VLC on this box loads its media-library meta-file instead of a CLI URL (config quirk) — a GUI/environment rabbit hole, not the hand-off. The dispatch mechanics are the actual fix. Let me verify the full installed-wrapper chain by instrumenting the player call and dispatching through the real handler via `gio open`:

input.command:
pkill -x vlc 2>/dev/null; pkill -f range-server.js 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.3
cat > /tmp/vlc-stub <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
{ echo "player-argv: $#"; i=1; for a in "$@"; do echo "  [$i] <$a>"; i=$((i+1)); done; } >> /tmp/player-args.log
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/vlc-stub

Reuses v1 structured filters (resolution/source/codec/indexer/min-seeders/size/regex), sort, cross-indexer grouping + "Show duplicates", count line, and 30-row "Load more".
242: - Actions (both types): friendly/advanced download → `POST S4`; `201` toast "Added to downloads"; `409` toast "Already downloading". Trash → confirm → `DELETE S6?deleteFiles=true`.
243: 
244: ### Screen: Player (`/watch/:infoHash`[`?episode=SxxExx`])
245: - Optional `?episode=SxxExx` (TV, season-pack downloads): after the S13 file list loads, auto-select the first file whose server-parsed `seasonNumber`/`episodeNumber` matches; no match → normal file-picker state.
246: - Playback is gated on completion (D8): a torrent that has no fully-downloaded video yet shows a *waiting* state with download % that reloads automatically once `streamable` flips true. `S7b` mode decision; `direct`/`remux-audio`/`transcode` `<video>`; `player-required` → "Open in your player" (`movie://`), "Download file", back; an always-visible **Player** topbar icon opens the current file in the local player; multi-file picker for packs (only completed files are listed).
247: - `playinfo` 404 → "No playable file yet" (or the waiting state above while the download runs).
248: 
249: ### Pages: Downloads (`/downloads`) and Settings (`/settings`)
250: - Downloads rows: 2:3 poster thumb (from the art volume), title (+ `S0NE0M` label when `seasonNumber/episodeNumber` set), grayscale quality + audio chip, progress bar, speed/ETA, actions **Watch · Player (S7 native, `movie://`) · Pause/Resume · Download file (S10) · Remove** (confirm → S6 `?deleteFiles=true`). Watch/Player are disabled until `streamable` (a fully-downloaded file exists). **Multiple copies of one movie are grouped under a single header** (`Movie · N versions`); each grouped row is labeled with its **version** (`audio · quality`, e.g. `PT · Dub · 1080p WEB-DL x264`) so copies that differ only by language or quality are distinguishable instead of looking like duplicates.
251: - Settings: existing System/Configuration/About cards + **Audio language** card + **Local player** card — platform-aware (`detectOs`): choose VLC/MPV/MPC-HC/PotPlayer on Windows, VLC/MPV on Linux (localStorage hint, `readPlayerPreference`); download the matching installer/uninstaller — `.cmd` (PowerShell, registers `movie://` under HKCU) on Windows, `.sh` (writes `movie-open.sh` + a `x-scheme-handler/movie` `.desktop` entry, registers via `xdg-mime`, auto-detects installed player via `command -v`/snap/flatpak) on Linux. No artwork settings exist (D21): cards have exactly one look and one source.
252: - Data for both: Socket.IO `downloads:initial` / `downloads:update` → Zustand store.

254: ### Grayscale state mapping (replaces §4.2 colors)
255: Monochrome chips only: `queued` #808080 outline, `fetching-metadata` #b3b3b3, `downloading` #fff + spinner, `stalled` #808080, `paused` #e5e5e5 outline, `checking` #b3b3b3, `seeding` #fff, `error` #fff on #000 border, `unknown` #555. No hue in any state.

258: - **ConfirmDownloadSheet (C-DL1):** every friendly download (movie / season / episode) first shows a sheet naming the exact pick — release title, resolution/source/codec, size, seeders, indexer — with `[Start]` and `[Advanced…]`. Sources resolve in the background (cache keyed `title|season|episode`, AbortController); while unresolved the CTA reads `Looking for best source…`. No silent auto-start.
259: - **Versions (D19):** copies of one movie collapse into a single library item. `lib/versions.ts` holds the pure helpers (playable, label `audio · quality`, and the default rule: **most recently completed playable copy**, tie-break higher resolution); `store/versionStore` persists the active copy per `movie:<tmdbId>` in `localStorage` so rails, the Downloads page and the Detail hero agree on which version **Watch** targets. input.newString:
- Errors: `404` unknown torrent / no complete streamable file.

### S7c External-player hand-off (`movie` scheme — frontend URL + OS registration)
- Hand-off URL (`frontend/src/api.ts` `externalPlayerHref`): the absolute HTTP stream URL `<origin>/api/stream/<hash>[?file=…]` written as an **opaque URI body** — `movie:http://…` — **never** `movie://http://…`. Browsers re-serialize every link through their URI parser before dispatching it to the OS handler, and a custom scheme cannot nest an `http://` URL in its authority: `movie://http://host/…` is canonicalized to `movie://http//host/…` (the inner scheme's colon is dropped because `http` is read as the `movie` host), so players received a schemeless relative path and VLC errored with a `file:///…` MRL. The opaque form has no authority to re-parse and round-trips unchanged.
- Normalization: the registered OS launcher strips a `movie:`/`movie://` prefix and repairs the browser-canonicalized `http//`/`https//` prefix before handing the URL to the player; anything that is not `http(s)://` is rejected and the player is never launched (`normalizeMovieHandoffUrl` in `frontend/src/lib/openerInstaller.ts` is the reference; the emitted Linux `sh` and Windows `ps1` launchers implement the same logic inline).
- Registration artifacts (Settings → Local player card):
  - Linux `install-movie-player.sh`: probes an installed player (`command -v`, then flatpak; preference first — VLC → MPV), writes `~/.local/share/movie-downloader/movie-open.sh` and `~/.local/share/applications/movie-downloader.desktop` (`Exec="…/movie-open.sh" %u`, `MimeType=x-scheme-handler/movie`), registers via `xdg-mime default … x-scheme-handler/movie`, then prints `Found: …` and `Verified: …` (checks `mimeapps.list`; `xdg-mime query` alone is unreliable under `dash` because its `command -v` cannot resolve absolute `Exec` paths). Idempotent re-run overwrites both files. `uninstall-movie-player.sh` removes the desktop entry, the launcher dir and the mimeapps association.
  - Windows `install-movie-player.cmd` (PowerShell bootstrap): probes known install paths (preference first among VLC/MPV/MPC-HC/PotPlayer), writes `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MovieDownloader\movie-open.ps1` and registers `HKCU:\Software\Classes\movie\shell\open\command` → `"…\powershell.exe" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -File "<launcher>" "%1"`. The handler invokes PowerShell **directly, never cmd.exe**, so `%XX` in the URL is not re-parsed by the shell; the launcher normalizes and `Start-Process`s the player. The script reads the key back and prints the result. `uninstall-movie-player.cmd` removes the key and both launcher files (incl. the legacy `movie-open.cmd`).
- Setup confirmation & Player gating: a web page cannot detect an OS registration, so Settings stores a user confirmation in `localStorage` (`SETUP_DONE_KEY`, shown as a status pill “Registered — confirmed by you” / “Not registered yet”). Until that confirmation is set, every **Player** action (rendered via `ExternalPlayerLink` on Watch/Downloads/Detail) routes to Settings with an explanatory toast instead of handing the link to the OS and failing silently in the player. Switching the chosen player clears the confirmation (the registered launcher is bound to the previously installed player until the installer is re-run).

### S8 `GET /api/images/tmdb/*path`

The hand-off is now an **opaque `movie:<absolute-url>`** (`api.ts externalPlayerHref`) that round-trips any parser unchanged, and both OS launchers normalize legacy shapes (`openerInstaller.normalizeMovieHandoffUrl`: strip `movie:`/`movie://`, repair `http//`/`https//`) and reject anything that isn't `http(s)://` so the player is never launched with garbage. Windows now registers a **PowerShell `.ps1` launcher** invoked directly via `powershell.exe -File` (never cmd.exe, so `%XX` in the URL is not re-parsed) and reads the registry key back to print success; the Linux installer quotes the desktop `Exec`, verifies via `mimeapps.list` (dash-safe), and is idempotent. Setup UX redesigned (Settings → Local player): explains what will be installed/registered and the expected `Found: …` / `Verified: …` output, offers Download/Copy installer + uninstaller, shows a registration status pill, and **Player actions gate to Settings** (`ExternalPlayerLink` on Watch/Downloads/Detail) until the user confirms — no more silent VLC failure. input.newString:
## Open movies in your local player (one-time setup)

Downloads play in the browser as soon as the file is fully downloaded. Codecs the browser can't
decode (4K/HEVC, exotic audio) show an **"Open in your player"** button instead. Browsers can't
launch desktop apps on their own, so the app uses a `movie://` link your machine must be told how to
open. The setup is **platform-aware** — you get the right installer for the OS you're on.

- Open **Settings → Local player**. The card explains exactly what the installer will do and what
  output to expect (`Found: …` → `Verified: movie:// links now open …`). Pick your player (VLC / MPV;
  MPC-HC / PotPlayer on Windows), then **Download installer** (or **Copy installer**).
- **Windows** — run the downloaded `.cmd` once on this computer (double-click is fine). It auto-locates
  the player (preference first), registers the `movie://` handler for your user under HKCU (no admin),
  and prints the result.
- **Linux** — run the downloaded `.sh` once in a terminal: `bash ~/Downloads/install-movie-player.sh`.
  It auto-detects your installed player (`vlc`/`mpv`, including flatpak), writes a small launcher +
  desktop entry, registers the handler via `xdg-mime`, and verifies the registration.
- Back in the app, mark **“I ran it — movie:// works”**. The **Player** buttons on the Watch,
  Downloads and Detail pages then open the file directly in your local player. Until you confirm,
  those buttons route you to Settings instead of failing silently.
- Re-running the installer is harmless (it just overwrites its two files). To remove the handler,
  download and run the matching **uninstaller**. Switching players in Settings only takes effect
  after you re-run the installer once.

Until it's registered, the **Download file** button is the fallback.

git commit -m "fix: make movie:// hand-off URL-safe and redesign local-player setup (T-001)

Root cause: the app emitted movie://http://localhost:5173/... for the Player
buttons. Browsers re-serialize every link through their URI parser before
handing it to the OS handler, and a custom scheme cannot nest an absolute
http URL in its authority — movie://http://host/... is canonicalized to
movie://http//host/... (inner scheme colon dropped, 'http' read as the movie
host). The wrapper stripped movie:// and VLC received a schemeless relative
path, producing the file:///home/... MRL error popup.

Fix (frontend/src/api.ts + frontend/src/lib/openerInstaller.ts):
- Build the hand-off as an opaque movie:<absolute-url> (externalPlayerHref)
  which round-trips the URI parser unchanged.
- Emitted Linux sh and Windows PowerShell launchers now normalize every
  legacy shape (strip movie:/movie://, repair http// / https//) and reject
  anything that is not http(s):// so a player is never launched with garbage.
- Windows registers a .ps1 launcher invoked via powershell.exe -File directly
  (never cmd.exe, so %XX in the URL is not re-parsed) and reads the registry
  key back to report success.
- Linux installer quotes the desktop Exec, verifies against mimeapps.list
  (xdg-mime query is dash-unreliable for absolute Exec paths), is idempotent.

Setup UX (frontend/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx + ExternalPlayerLink): the
Local player card explains what will be installed/registered and the expected
Found:/Verified: output, offers Download/Copy installer + uninstaller, tracks a
registration confirmation (SETUP_DONE_KEY) with a status pill, and every Player
action routes to Settings with an explanation until setup is confirmed instead
of failing silently in VLC. Switching the chosen player clears the confirmation
(the registered launcher keeps opening the previously installed player).

Docs (00-index changelog, 02-specs S7c, README) updated; tests extended
(normalizer shapes, URL round-trip, gating, Settings flow)." 2>&1 | tail -6

part.text:
Done. Committed as `ecd6946` on `ticket/T-001`; the tree is clean.

## What was wrong (root cause, confirmed)

The frontend handed players `movie://http://localhost:5173/api/stream/<hash>`. I reproduced that **every browser re-serializes a link through its URI parser before OS dispatch**, and a custom scheme cannot nest an absolute `http://` URL in its authority: `new URL("movie://http://localhost:5173/…")` canonicalizes to `movie://http//localhost:5173/…` — the inner scheme's colon is dropped because `http` is parsed as the `movie` host. The registered wrapper stripped `movie://` and passed VLC a schemeless relative path, which VLC resolved to the `file:///home/gustavo/http//localhost%3A5173/…` MRL from the ticket. The OS-layer registration itself was fine (verified via `xdg-mime`/`gio` in a clean session env).

## What changed

- **URL construction (`api.ts`):** hand-off is now an opaque `movie:<absolute-stream-url>` (`externalPlayerHref`) that round-trips any URI parser unchanged. `movie://` references in Watch/Downloads/Detail all go through it.
- **Normalizer (`openerInstaller.ts` `normalizeMovieHandoffUrl`):** strips `movie:`/`movie://`, repairs the browser-canonicalized `http//`/`https//` prefix, and rejects anything not `http(s)://` — a player can never again be launched with a garbage path. The emitted Linux `sh` and Windows `ps1` launchers implement the same logic inline.
- **Windows:** the installer now writes a `.ps1` launcher registered via `powershell.exe -File … "%1"` (invoked directly, never `cmd.exe`, so `%XX` in URLs is not re-parsed) and reads the registry key back to print success; uninstaller also cleans the legacy `.cmd`.
- **Linux:** installer prints `Found:`/`Verified:`, quotes the desktop `Exec`, verifies via `mimeapps.list` (dash-safe), is idempotent; uninstaller confirms removal.
- **Setup UX + Player gating:** Settings → Local player now explains exactly what gets installed/registered and the expected output, offers Download/Copy installer + uninstaller, and shows a status pill backed by a localStorage confirmation (`SETUP_DONE_KEY`). Until confirmed, every **Player** action (`ExternalPlayerLink` on Watch/Downloads/Detail) routes to Settings with a toast instead of failing silently in VLC. Switching the player clears confirmation (launcher is bound to the previously installed player until re-run).
- **Docs:** `docs/plan/02-specs.md` new §S7c, `00-index.md` changelog row, README.

## Verification

- **Root cause:** reproduced exactly — `new URL('movie://http://localhost:5173/x').href === 'movie://http//localhost:5173/x'`, while the new opaque form round-trips.
- **Real machine (this box):** ran the generated installer (idempotent; prints `Found: VLC (/usr/bin/vlc)` + `Verified:`), then dispatched through the *actual* registered handler with `gio open` for the new opaque form, the legacy `movie://` form, and the broken canonicalized form — all three reached the player as a clean `http://…/api/stream/…` URL (query/percent-encoding intact). Uninstall → default gone + files removed, reinstall from clean state → re-registered (AC2 fully verified).
- **Checks:** frontend `typecheck`, `lint`, `npm test` (137 tests) and `npm run build` all green; backend (untouched) typecheck/lint/281 tests green. Tests added: normalizer shapes, URL parser round-trip regression guard, Player-link gating, Settings flow.

## Not fully verifiable in this session

- **AC1/AC4 visual "VLC opens, streams, is seekable"** for a real 4K file: the backend/Postgres stack isn't running and VLC on this box has a desktop-config/media-library quirk that made headless GUI automation unreliable. The chain now provably hands VLC the exact HTTP stream URL the browser already plays (the only thing that was broken); a human click on a real stream is the remaining check. The author's machine is left in the **registered** state so a Player click after confirming in Settings works.
- **AC3 Windows:** code-level parity is implemented and unit-tested; the documented manual checklist for a Windows box still needs author sign-off (as the ticket accepts).
